steps: Identify which equation: p = F/A (solid surface) or p = hρg (liquid)
Convert all units: cm² → m² (÷10,000), cm → m (÷100), g → kg (÷1000)
For total pressure at depth: add atmospheric pressure (101,000 Pa)
method_card.title: Pressure in Fluids
method_card.content:
Two pressure equations, so pick the right one for the situation.

Solid on a surface: \(p = \frac{F}{A}\). The force is the object's weight; the area is the contact area. For MAXIMUM pressure, use the smallest face.

Liquid at a depth: \(p = h\rho g\). Depth in metres, density in kg/m³.

Units: cm to m divide by 100; cm² to m² divide by 10,000. For total pressure in a liquid, add atmospheric pressure (about 101,000 Pa). 1 kPa = 1000 Pa.
method_card.example:
Solve: a 300 N box rests on 0.06 m².

\(p = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{300}{0.06} = 5000\) Pa.

exam_context.frequency: Common: pressure appears on most Paper 1 exams

gold.display: A diver is 25 m below the surface of the sea (density 1025 kg/m³). Calculate the total pressure on the diver. Atmospheric pressure = 101,000 Pa. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Liquid pressure = 25 × 1025 × 9.8 = 251,125 Pa. Total = 101,000 + 251,125 = 352,125 Pa. Forgetting atmospheric leaves 251,125.
Use seawater 1025 kg/m³, not fresh water 1000. Total = 101,000 + (25 × 1025 × 9.8) = 352,125 Pa. Using 1000 gives 346,000.

gold.hint: Find the liquid pressure with hρg (seawater density 1025), then add atmospheric pressure.

guided_steps.say: Total pressure = atmospheric + liquid. Use seawater density 1025 kg/m³. \(h = 25\) m, \(g = 9.8\).

guided_steps.hint: Add the 101,000 Pa of air on the surface.
Subtract atmospheric to recover the liquid pressure.
guided_steps.done: That is the liquid pressure back, so 352,125 Pa is right.

gold.display: A cuboid of mass 20 kg has dimensions 0.5 m × 0.2 m × 0.1 m. Calculate the maximum pressure it can exert on the floor. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: For MAXIMUM pressure use the SMALLEST face (0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 m²): p = 196 ÷ 0.02 = 9800 Pa. Using the largest face (0.1 m²) gives 1960.
The force is the weight, not the mass. Weight = 20 × 9.8 = 196 N, then p = 196 ÷ 0.02 = 9800 Pa. Using 20 N gives 1000 Pa.

gold.hint: Work out the weight first, then divide by the smallest face for maximum pressure.

guided_steps.say: Two steps: weight first, then pressure on the SMALLEST face for maximum pressure. \(W = mg\), then \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\).

guided_steps.hint: Mass × g.
The smallest face uses the two smallest sides: 0.2 × 0.1.
Answer × area gives the weight back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 196 N weight, so 9800 Pa is right.

gold.display: A dam holds back water 40 m deep. Calculate the force on a gate at the bottom of the dam that is 2 m wide and 1.5 m tall. Use the pressure at the full 40 m depth. (density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Pressure at 40 m = 40 × 1000 × 9.8 = 392,000 Pa. Force = pressure × area = 392,000 × 3 = 1,176,000 N. Stopping at the pressure gives 392,000.

gold.hint: Find the pressure at 40 m with hρg, then multiply by the gate area.

guided_steps.say: Two steps: pressure at 40 m, then force on the gate. \(p = h\rho g\), then \(F = pA\). \(\rho = 1000\).

guided_steps.hint: Width × height.
Pressure × area.
Force ÷ area gives the pressure at 40 m back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the pressure at 40 m, so 1,176,000 N is right.

gold.display: In a hydraulic system, the small piston has an area of 0.002 m² and the large piston has an area of 0.04 m². A force of 50 N is applied to the small piston. Calculate the force exerted by the large piston.

misconceptions.message: Pressure = 50 ÷ 0.002 = 25,000 Pa. Force on large piston = 25,000 × 0.04 = 1000 N. Stopping at the pressure leaves 25,000.
The large piston has the LARGER area, so the force is MULTIPLIED: F = 50 × (0.04 ÷ 0.002) = 1000 N. Inverting the ratio gives 50 × 0.05 = 2.5.

gold.hint: Find the fluid pressure from the small piston, then multiply by the large piston's area.

guided_steps.say: Pressure is the same throughout the fluid. Find it from the small piston, then apply it to the large one. \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\), then \(F = pA\).

guided_steps.hint: Same pressure × the larger area.
Large force ÷ large area gives the fluid pressure back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the fluid pressure, so 1000 N is right.

gold.display: A tank contains oil with a density of 800 kg/m³. At what depth does the pressure due to the oil equal atmospheric pressure (101,000 Pa)? Give your answer to 1 decimal place. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: h = p ÷ (ρg) = 101,000 ÷ (800 × 9.8) = 101,000 ÷ 7840 = 12.9 m. Dividing by ρ only (forgetting g) gives 126.3.
Use oil's density 800 kg/m³. h = 101,000 ÷ (800 × 9.8) = 12.9 m. Using water (1000) gives 10.3 m.

gold.hint: Rearrange to h = p over ρg, using oil's density 800.

guided_steps.say: Rearranged for depth, \(h = \dfrac{p}{\rho g}\). Use oil's density 800 kg/m³. \(p = 101000\) Pa, to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.hint: Depth × ρg returns about the atmospheric pressure.
guided_steps.done: That is about 101,000 Pa (the small gap is rounding), so 12.9 m is right.

gold.display: A submarine is 200 m below the surface of the sea (density of seawater = 1025 kg/m³). Calculate the total pressure on the hull in kPa. Atmospheric pressure = 101,000 Pa. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Liquid pressure = 200 × 1025 × 9.8 = 2,009,000 Pa. Total = 101,000 + 2,009,000 = 2,110,000 Pa = 2110 kPa. Forgetting atmospheric gives 2009 kPa.
Convert Pa to kPa by ÷1000: 2,110,000 Pa = 2110 kPa. Leaving it in Pa gives 2,110,000.

gold.hint: Add atmospheric to the liquid pressure, then divide by 1000 for kPa.

guided_steps.say: Total pressure, then convert to kPa. \(p = p_{atm} + h\rho g\), then ÷1000. \(h = 200\) m, \(\rho = 1025\), \(g = 9.8\).

guided_steps.hint: Add the surface air pressure.
1 kPa = 1000 Pa, so divide by 1000.
kPa × 1000 gives the total in Pa back.
guided_steps.done: That is the total in Pa, so 2110 kPa is right.

bronze.display: A box weighing 200 N rests on the floor. The area of the base is 0.04 m². Calculate the pressure on the floor.

misconceptions.message: Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 ÷ 0.04 = 5000 Pa. Multiplying gives 8, which is far too small.

guided_steps.say: A solid pushing on a surface uses \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\). Force \(F = 200\) N, area \(A = 0.04\) m².

guided_steps.pre: The area is already in m², so write A =
guided_steps.hint: It is given as 0.04 m², no conversion needed.
Dividing by 0.04 is the same as multiplying by 25: 200 × 25.
Answer × area should return the 200 N force.
guided_steps.done: That returns the 200 N force, so 5000 Pa is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the pressure at the bottom of a 2 m deep swimming pool. The density of water is 1000 kg/m³. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
bronze.equation_hint: Given on equation sheet: \(p = h\rho g\)

misconceptions.message: Use p = hρg. Do not stop at h × ρ = 2000; multiply by g too: 2 × 1000 × 9.8 = 19,600 Pa.

guided_steps.say: Pressure in a liquid uses \(p = h\rho g\). Depth \(h = 2\) m, density \(\rho = 1000\) kg/m³, \(g = 9.8\) N/kg.

guided_steps.hint: Undo the two multiplications to get the depth back.
guided_steps.done: That returns the 2 m depth, so 19,600 Pa is right.

bronze.display: A pressure of 40,000 Pa acts over an area of 0.1 m². Calculate the force.

misconceptions.message: F = p × A = 40,000 × 0.1 = 4000 N. Dividing gives 400,000, which is the slip.

guided_steps.say: Rearranged, \(F = p \times A\). Pressure \(p = 40000\) Pa, area \(A = 0.1\) m².

guided_steps.pre: Write the area in m²: A =
guided_steps.hint: Given as 0.1 m² already.
Multiplying by 0.1 is dividing by 10.
Force ÷ area should give the pressure back.
guided_steps.done: That returns the 40,000 Pa, so 4000 N is right.

bronze.display: A crate weighing 500 N rests on the ground with a base area of 0.05 m². Calculate the pressure.

misconceptions.message: p = F ÷ A = 500 ÷ 0.05 = 10,000 Pa. Multiplying gives 25, far too small.

guided_steps.say: Solid on a surface: \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\). Weight \(F = 500\) N, area \(A = 0.05\) m².

guided_steps.hint: Given as 0.05 m².
Dividing by 0.05 is multiplying by 20.
Answer × area should give the 500 N force.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 500 N weight, so 10,000 Pa is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 5 m in water. Density of water = 1000 kg/m³. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
bronze.equation_hint: Given on equation sheet: \(p = h\rho g\)

misconceptions.message: Use p = hρg. Do not stop at 5 × 1000 = 5000; multiply by g: 5 × 1000 × 9.8 = 49,000 Pa.

guided_steps.say: Liquid pressure: \(p = h\rho g\). \(h = 5\) m, \(\rho = 1000\) kg/m³, \(g = 9.8\).

guided_steps.hint: Undo the multiplications to recover the depth.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 5 m depth, so 49,000 Pa is right.

bronze.display: A 600 N force creates a pressure of 3000 Pa. Calculate the area over which it acts.

misconceptions.message: A = F ÷ p = 600 ÷ 3000 = 0.2 m². Multiplying gives 1,800,000, which is impossible for an area.

guided_steps.say: Rearranged for area, \(A = \dfrac{F}{p}\). Force \(F = 600\) N, pressure \(p = 3000\) Pa.

guided_steps.pre: Write the pressure in Pa: p =
guided_steps.hint: Given as 3000 Pa.
Force ÷ area should give the pressure back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 3000 Pa, so 0.2 m² is right.

bronze.display: The pressure at the bottom of a column of liquid is 29,400 Pa. The density is 1000 kg/m³. Calculate the depth. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: h = p ÷ (ρg). Divide by both ρ AND g: 29,400 ÷ (1000 × 9.8) = 3 m. Dividing by 1000 only gives 29.4 m.

guided_steps.say: Rearranged for depth, \(h = \dfrac{p}{\rho g}\). \(p = 29400\) Pa, \(\rho = 1000\), \(g = 9.8\).

guided_steps.hint: Depth × ρg should give the pressure back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 29,400 Pa, so 3 m is right.

bronze.display: A pressure of 800 Pa acts on an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the force.

misconceptions.message: F = p × A = 800 × 0.5 = 400 N. Dividing gives 1600, which is the slip.

guided_steps.say: \(F = p \times A\). Pressure \(p = 800\) Pa, area \(A = 0.5\) m².

guided_steps.hint: Given as 0.5 m².
Multiplying by 0.5 is halving.
Force ÷ area gives the pressure back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 800 Pa, so 400 N is right.

silver.display: A person weighing 300 N stands on a surface 20 cm × 50 cm. Calculate the pressure in Pa. (Give your answer as a whole number.)

misconceptions.message: Convert to metres first: 0.20 × 0.50 = 0.1 m², so p = 300 ÷ 0.1 = 3000 Pa. Using 20 × 50 = 1000 (cm²) gives 0.3, which is wrong.

guided_steps.say: Solid on a surface: \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\). The dimensions are in cm, so convert to metres first.

guided_steps.hint: Divide by 100.
Divide by 100.
Multiply the two sides in metres.
Dividing by 0.1 is × 10.
Answer × area gives the 300 N force.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 300 N, so 3000 Pa is right.

silver.display: A column of mercury (density 13,600 kg/m³) is 0.8 m tall. Calculate the pressure at the bottom in Pa. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
silver.equation_hint: Given on equation sheet: \(p = h\rho g\)

misconceptions.message: Use mercury's density 13,600 kg/m³, not water's 1000. p = 0.8 × 13,600 × 9.8 = 106,624 Pa. Using 1000 gives 7840.

guided_steps.say: Liquid pressure: \(p = h\rho g\). Use mercury's density, 13,600 kg/m³, not water. \(h = 0.8\) m.

guided_steps.hint: Undo the multiplications to recover the height.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 0.8 m, so 106,624 Pa is right.

silver.display: Calculate the total pressure on a diver at 10 m depth in water (density 1000 kg/m³). Include atmospheric pressure of 101,000 Pa. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Liquid pressure = 10 × 1000 × 9.8 = 98,000 Pa. Add atmospheric: 101,000 + 98,000 = 199,000 Pa. Forgetting it leaves 98,000.

guided_steps.say: Total pressure = atmospheric + liquid: \(p = p_{atm} + h\rho g\). \(h = 10\) m, \(\rho = 1000\), \(g = 9.8\).

guided_steps.hint: Add the 101,000 Pa of air pressure on top.
Subtract atmospheric to recover the liquid pressure.
guided_steps.done: That is the liquid pressure back, so 199,000 Pa total is right.

silver.display: A nail pushes with a force of 50 N. The point of the nail has an area of 2 cm². Calculate the pressure in Pa.

misconceptions.message: Convert cm² to m² by ÷10,000: 2 cm² = 0.0002 m². p = 50 ÷ 0.0002 = 250,000 Pa. Dividing by 100 instead gives 2500.

guided_steps.say: Solid on a surface: \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\). The area is in cm², so convert to m² first.

guided_steps.hint: 1 m² = 10,000 cm², so divide by 10,000.
Answer × area gives the 50 N force.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 50 N force, so 250,000 Pa is right.

silver.display: The pressure at the bottom of a tank of liquid is 34,300 Pa. The depth is 3.5 m. Calculate the density of the liquid. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: ρ = p ÷ (hg) = 34,300 ÷ (3.5 × 9.8) = 34,300 ÷ 34.3 = 1000 kg/m³. Dividing by h only (forgetting g) gives 9800.

guided_steps.say: Rearranged for density, \(\rho = \dfrac{p}{hg}\). \(p = 34300\) Pa, \(h = 3.5\) m, \(g = 9.8\).

guided_steps.hint: Density × hg should give the pressure back.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 34,300 Pa, so 1000 kg/m³ is right.

silver.display: Calculate the difference in pressure between a depth of 3 m and 8 m in water (density 1000 kg/m³). (g = 9.8 N/kg)
silver.equation_hint: Given on equation sheet: \(p = h\rho g\)

misconceptions.message: Use the depth difference: Δh = 8 − 3 = 5 m. Δp = 5 × 1000 × 9.8 = 49,000 Pa. Using 8 m instead of the difference gives 78,400.

guided_steps.say: Pressure difference uses the depth difference in \(p = h\rho g\). \(\Delta h = 8 − 3\).

guided_steps.hint: The extra depth between the two points.
Undo the multiplications to recover the depth difference.
guided_steps.done: Returns the 5 m difference, so 49,000 Pa is right.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One pressure equation, values already in the right units (m, m², N, Pa). Pick p = F/A or p = hρg and substitute straight in.
problem_bank.silver_description: Convert units first (cm to m, cm² to m²) or rearrange the equation for the unknown before you substitute.
problem_bank.gold_description: Two steps chained: a weight or liquid pressure first, then add atmospheric pressure, work a hydraulic system, or convert the result.

worked_examples.question: A box weighing 200 N rests on the floor. The area of the base is 0.04 m². Calculate the pressure on the floor.
A column of mercury is 0.8 m tall. The density of mercury is 13,600 kg/m³. Calculate the pressure at the bottom of the column. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A diver is 25 m below the surface of the sea. The density of seawater is 1025 kg/m³. Calculate the total pressure on the diver. (g = 9.8 N/kg, atmospheric pressure = 101,000 Pa)

bronze.title: Bronze: one equation, straight in
steps: Pick the equation from the situation: a solid on a surface uses \(p = \frac{F}{A}\); a liquid at a depth uses \(p = h\rho g\).
The values are already in the right units (m, m², N, Pa), so substitute straight in and calculate.
State the answer with its unit (Pa, N, or m), then check by working backwards.

example.question: A 240 N box rests on the floor on an area of 0.6 m². Find the pressure.

silver.title: Silver: convert or rearrange first
steps: If lengths are in cm, convert before substituting: cm to m divide by 100, cm² to m² divide by 10,000.
If the unknown is not the subject, rearrange first: \(A = \frac{F}{p}\), \(h = \frac{p}{\rho g}\), \(\rho = \frac{p}{hg}\).
Then substitute and calculate as in Bronze, and check backwards.

example.question: A force of 8 N acts on a 25 cm × 20 cm face. Find the pressure in Pa.

gold.title: Gold: two steps chained
steps: Break the problem into two calculations. Common chains: weight then pressure, liquid pressure then force, or pressure then unit convert.
For total pressure in a liquid, add atmospheric pressure (about 101,000 Pa) to \(h\rho g\).
Work the first step, feed its result into the second, then check backwards.

example.question: A diver is 15 m deep in fresh water (density 1000 kg/m³). Atmospheric pressure = 101,000 Pa. Find the total pressure. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

opener.label: Before any equation
opener.display:
An elephant weighs 40,000 N, spread over 0.4 m² of feet.
A woman weighs 500 N, balanced on 0.0002 m² of heel tips.
Who presses harder on each square metre of floor?

steps.say: No equation yet, just share each weight over its area. Elephant first:

steps.hint: Share 500 N over a tiny 0.0002 m²: 500 ÷ 0.0002.

steps.say: The woman, at 2,500,000 Pa against the elephant's 100,000 Pa. A slim heel can dent a wooden floor an elephant would not mark, because the same force squeezed through a tiny area makes huge pressure. That is exactly \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\): pressure is force ÷ area.

bronze.display: Find the pressure at the bottom of a 3 m deep freshwater lake. Density of water = 1000 kg/m³. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
bronze.label: Together: your first one

steps.say: A liquid at a depth, so use \(p = h\rho g\). Depth 3 m, density 1000, g = 9.8. Take it one multiply at a time.

steps.hint: Undo the multiplies to get the depth back.
steps.done: Returns the 3 m depth, so 29,400 Pa is right.

silver.display: A tile weighing 8 N rests flat on a 25 cm × 20 cm face. Find the pressure on the floor in Pa.
silver.label: Together: the silver move

steps.say: Solid on a surface: \(p = \dfrac{F}{A}\). The sides are in cm, so convert to metres before finding the area.

steps.hint: Answer × area gives the 8 N force.
steps.done: Returns the 8 N, so 160 Pa is right.

gold.display: A diver is 15 m below the surface of a freshwater lake (density 1000 kg/m³). Atmospheric pressure = 101,000 Pa. Calculate the total pressure on the diver. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
gold.label: Together: the gold move

steps.say: Two steps: liquid pressure with \(p = h\rho g\), then add atmospheric. Build the liquid pressure one multiply at a time.

steps.hint: Subtract atmospheric to recover the liquid pressure.
steps.done: That is the liquid pressure back, so 248,000 Pa total is right.
